experiments.name: Stability study request: ibuprofen 200 mg tablets F-101 to F-103
experiments.description: 3 formulations x 3 conditions x 5 timepoints. Teams generate containers, locations and tasks from this.

texts.name: Purpose
texts.html: Support shelf-life assignment for three ibuprofen 200 mg tablet formulations (F-101 wet granulation, F-102 direct compression, F-103 direct compression with 2% crospovidone) under ICH Q1A(R2) long-term, intermediate and accelerated conditions.

texts.name: Study design
texts.html:
Conditions

  • 25 °C / 60% RH (long term)
  • 30 °C / 65% RH (intermediate)
  • 40 °C / 75% RH (accelerated)

Timepoints

T0, 1, 3, 6 and 12 months (accelerated: T0, 1, 3, 6 months only). Study start: 2026-10-21.

Tests per timepoint

TestMethodDestructiveUnits per test
AppearanceVisual, SOP-QC-001No10 tablets
Assay and related substancesHPLC, SOP-QC-014Yes10 tablets
DissolutionUSP II, 50 rpm, pH 7.2Yes6 tablets
Water contentKarl Fischer, SOP-QC-022Yes5 tablets
HardnessTablet testerYes10 tablets

Non-destructive tests reuse the same container and return it to its chamber. Destructive tests consume a dedicated container per timepoint.

experiments.name: Step 1: Suzuki coupling to 4-cyanobiphenyl
experiments.description: Completed step 1. Its product is the reactant of step 2 (for teams to create).

texts.name: Purpose
texts.html: Prepare 4-cyanobiphenyl as the intermediate for biphenyl-4-carboxylic acid (step 2: nitrile hydrolysis).

texts.name: Procedure
texts.html:
1. Charge 4-bromobenzonitrile (1.82 g, 10.0 mmol), phenylboronic acid (1.46 g, 12.0 mmol) and K2CO3 (2.76 g, 20.0 mmol) to a 100 mL flask.
  2. Add toluene (40 mL) and water (10 mL). Degas with N2 for 15 min.
  3. Add Pd(PPh3)4 (0.23 g, 2 mol%). Heat to 90 °C for 4 h.
  4. Cool to room temperature, separate layers, wash organics with brine, dry over MgSO4, concentrate.
  5. Recrystallise from ethanol.

texts.name: Conclusion
texts.html: Isolated 1.54 g (86%) of 4-cyanobiphenyl as a white solid. LCMS purity 99.1% (254 nm), m/z 180.1 [M+H]+. Proceed to step 2.

experiments.name: Step 1: amide coupling to N-benzylbenzamide
experiments.description: A second, independent starting point for the step linker.

texts.name: Purpose
texts.html: Prepare N-benzylbenzamide from benzoic acid and benzylamine.

texts.name: Procedure
texts.html:
1. Dissolve benzoic acid (1.22 g, 10.0 mmol) in DCM (30 mL). Add EDC·HCl (2.30 g, 12.0 mmol) and HOBt (1.62 g, 12.0 mmol). Stir 15 min at 0 °C.
  2. Add benzylamine (1.18 g, 11.0 mmol) and triethylamine (2.8 mL, 20 mmol). Stir 16 h at room temperature.
  3. Wash with 1 M HCl, sat. NaHCO3, brine. Dry, concentrate.

experiments.name: Grignard addition: triphenylmethanol from benzophenone
experiments.description: Exothermic, moisture-sensitive, ether solvent: a hazard review and a timed procedure.

texts.name: Purpose
texts.html: Prepare triphenylmethanol by addition of phenylmagnesium bromide to benzophenone.

texts.name: Procedure
texts.html:
1. Flame-dry a 250 mL three-neck flask under N2. Add magnesium turnings (0.29 g, 12.0 mmol) and one crystal of iodine.
  2. Add 5 mL of a solution of bromobenzene (1.73 g, 11.0 mmol) in anhydrous THF (20 mL). Warm gently until initiation (colour fades, reflux starts). Wait 5 min.
  3. Add the rest of the bromobenzene solution dropwise over 20 min to keep a gentle reflux.
  4. Reflux for 30 min. Cool to 0 °C in an ice bath for 10 min.
  5. Add benzophenone (1.82 g, 10.0 mmol) in THF (15 mL) dropwise over 15 min, keeping the internal temperature below 10 °C.
  6. Stir 1 h at room temperature.
  7. Quench slowly with saturated NH4Cl (30 mL) at 0 °C. Stir 10 min.
  8. Extract with diethyl ether (3 × 30 mL), dry over MgSO4, concentrate. Recrystallise from hexane.
